stem: Why does checking `typeof value === 'object'` fail to narrow a `string[] | null` union down to just `string[]`?
options: In JavaScript, `typeof null` evaluates to the string `'object'`, so `null` remains in the narrowed union.
JavaScript considers `null` to be undefined unless strict mode is enabled in the compiler.
TypeScript requires `Array.isArray()` to be invoked before any `typeof` operator can be parsed.
TypeScript ignores `typeof` guards unless the value is strictly an object literal.
objective: Explain why typeof null evaluates to 'object' and how to safely narrow null from object unions

stem: You have a variable `input` with type `string | null | undefined`. Which check safely narrows `input` to just `string` in a single comparison?
